 Judgment

This miscellaneous second appeal, under section 71(6) of Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006 (for short "FSSA") has been filed against the judgment dated 15/5/2025 passed by Principal District Judge, Gwalior/ Appellate Authority in RCA No. 93/2025, as well as, order dated 27/12/2024 passed by Adjudicating Officer/Additional District Magistrate Gwalior in case No. Q/Food safety/05/2024.

entities.text: Principal District Judge, Gwalior/ Appellate Authority
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: It is not out of place to mention here that the Adjudicating Officer had imposed a penalty of Rs.3,00,000/- after holding the appellant guilty under section 51 of FSSA.
The appellate Authority has reduced the penalty from Rs.3,00,000/- to Rs.1,50,000/-.

2. Facts necessary for disposal of present appeal, in short, are that a complaint was filed before the Adjudicating Officer contending that on 16/6/2023, at about 1:00 p.m., the Food Safety Officer had inspected the Firm M/s Hanuman Dairy.
Appellant No.1 was present at the time of inspection and he disclosed that Ravi Lodhi is the proprietor, who is his elder brother.

During inspection, it was found that 2 kg of Paneer and 5 kg of Mawa were kept in loose NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2025:MPHC-GWL:30978 2 MSA-33-2025 condition.
The sample of Mawa and Paneer were taken by the Food Safety Officer with consent of appellant No.1.
After completing the formalities, the sealed samples were sent to Food Laboratory, Bhopal.
As per the reports (Ex.P/15 and P/19), both the samples were found to be substandard.

Thereafter a notice under section 46(4) of FSSA was given thereby intimating the appellants that they can file an appeal against the report of Food Vikash Lodhi vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 21 November, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/38666752/
1 Analyst, but they did not file any appeal.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The sanction for prosecution was obtained and accordingly complaint was filed.
3. Appellants appeared before the Adjudicating Officer and refuted the allegations and claimed that they had not committed any offence and no raid was conducted in their premises.
The Adjudicating Officer, after completing the inquiry, held that appellants were guilty of committing offence under section 26 read with section 51 of FSSA and imposed a penalty of Rs. 3,00,000/-.
As already pointed out, the Appellate Authority/Principal District Judge, Gwalior has reduced the penalty from Rs.3,00,000/- to Rs.1,50,000/-.
4. It is the case of appellants that the appellants are petty traders and the penalty amount may be reduced.

5. Heard the learned counsel for the appellants.
6.
Whether a person is a petty trader or not will not make any difference while assessing the question of penalty.
Sale of substandard food articles cannot be appreciated.
From the record of the Adjudicating Officer, it is clear that the appellants did not lead any evidence in support of their defence.
7. No other argument is advanced by counsel for appellants.

8. Considering the totality of facts and circumstances of the case, coupled with the fact that Paneer and Mawa were found to be of substandard quality, no NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2025:MPHC-GWL:30978 3 MSA-33-2025 case is made out warranting interference.
9. Appeal fails and is hereby dismissed.

(G. S. AHLUWALIA) JUDGE (and)
